analysis:
This batch has two changes. ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift head line 155 adds a call to acceptPendingClusterUpdateDrain(from: mailbox) in the lifecycle monitor loop. ProviderLoop.swift (head 566-569) adds two state fields, clusterUpdateDrainID and clusterUpdateDrainTask. The implementation, ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain.swift, is not in this batch, so its behavior is unverified.

The new call reads from the same owner-only lifecycle mailbox (the TB-012 operator mailbox) used by the model-switch and add-on control paths. The visible siblings validate requests against ProcessIdentity with request.isValid(for: identity) (lines 148-149 and 162). Whether the cluster-update-drain claim performs equivalent identity and request-id validation must be checked in the new file.

Questions for integration:
- A drain that "holds" admission could keep a provider out of routing, affecting availability (A-018; similar to the T-059/T-060 local hold DoS class). Confirm it is bounded, released on cancel, and cannot reopen admission owned by .lifecycle or .addonHold. See the beginServingDrain owner checks at line 12 and the drained transitions at lines 118/121.
- It awaits on the monitor loop rather than spawning a Task. If it blocks, it could stall handling of lifecycle stop requests (lines 148-151). This availability concern needs checking.
- Interaction with shutdownStoppedClusterMember (line 180) and drainAndShutdown (line 193) when clusterUpdateDrainTask is active.

No regression is identified from the visible lines. These are additive state fields and a monitor hook. Plaintext handling, keys, attestation and App Attest worker retirement (line 113) are unchanged here.
